For a closed ambient cap, every fiber not wholly contained provides a point with strictly negative affine margin. Any anchored convex combination of such points would stay strictly negative and belong to the captured own fiber. Thus the bad bases have convex hull disjoint from p, and strict separation supplies an admissible base trace wholly captured by the cap. The empty bad set yields the total mass; rank zero has only the whole-base trace.

With symmetric positive definite Sigma, covariance duality gives the direction minus Sigma inverse times a farthest displacement, divided by R. Its Gamma norm is one and its evaluation at that point is minus R. If delta is smaller, the open excluded side contains a positive-volume subset of the own body, by interpolation with an interior point and then a small interior ball.

A base minimizer exists among finitely many traces. Tightening through p removes only bases, and cannot lower the mass below the minimum. Finitely many nonzero drifts and bounded fiber evaluations permit one finite tilt multiplier making positive-drift fibers full and negative-drift fibers empty. The p-fiber is on zero drift and strictly loses volume, with no gains possible on other zero-drift fibers. This also works for a zero base normal and rank zero.

If delta is at least R, including equality, Cauchy–Schwarz gives every own trace full and the capture bound excludes any improvement on atomic depth. An admissible pure-base trace attains equality. Under a strict gap a minimizing cap cannot be pure-base or contain the whole own fiber. It contains an own-interior neighborhood of y by the positive buffer, so its cutting plane meets own interior.
